cases.note: Most polls. §11’s loop asks the same question every few seconds and the answer is usually the document the robot already has — so `adopt` is true and `changed` is false, and a caller that could not tell the two apart would rewrite the desired state on every tick.
What the loop exists for. Adopted, and it changes something.

§33.8 says a robot never invents a desired state; this is the step before that, where a response is stopped from *becoming* one. The robot carries on against what it has, which is what it does whenever it cannot reach the Hub at all — so a garbage response costs it nothing that being offline does not.

cases.note: The case this file was written for. A Hub serving two documents under one generation has broken the property §11 rests idempotence on, and the robot is the only party that can see it. Refused, because adopting would have the robot running new software while reporting the old generation applied — and a fleet console would show it converged, which is exactly the claim §17 forbids and is invisible because every robot looks right.
cases.expected: {"adopt":false,"changed":false,"faults":[{"code":"generation_reused","message":"The Hub is serving a different document under generation 41, which this robot has already applied. §11 rests idempotence on that counter, so adopting this would have the robot running new software while reporting the old generation as applied — and a fleet console would show it converged. Bump the generation on the Hub and this robot will take it on the next poll.","severity":"error"}],"generation":41}

cases.note: The same document against a robot with nothing running. Not news, and not reported — a finding that fired on every idle robot would be one nobody reads.

Nothing held, so there is no digest to compare and no generation to have gone backwards. It must not report a reuse, which is what a naive comparison against an empty digest would do — and it must report `changed`, because everything is a change to a robot that had nothing.
A backup restore that also emptied the robot. Both are reported and both are adopted; the ordering of the list is frozen so an operator gets one list rather than one per poll.
